title: Fix token-splitting edge cases and template markers during model onboarding
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Summary:
During recent model onboarding runs we observed a class of failures and subtle regressions caused by tokenizer edge cases interacting with chat template markers. These issues appear for new model variants where tokenization semantics changed (subtoken boundaries, grapheme clusters, and special marker handling) and for templates that assume a single-token role delimiter. The result: (1) mismatch in token counts for pinned model versions vs. runtime tokenizer, (2) generation off-by-one in prefix caching, and (3) degraded latency due to unexpected byte-level normalization.

Goal:
1) Detect and fix tokenizer->chat template incompatibilities during onboarding so model profiles published to the catalog are correct.
2) Add automated tokenizer compatibility checks to the onboarding pipeline and surface a tokenization_overhead metric in performance profiles.
3) Implement a minimal shim/fallback to preserve SLOs and avoid rollback-triggering tokenization mismatches for customers who pin model versions.

Scope and out-of-band constraints:
- This ticket focuses on onboarding-time checks and short-term shims. Long-term tokenizer migration and model retraining are out of scope.
- Must be backwards-compatible: do not change existing templates used by live customers without clear migration steps.

Risks:
- A naive shim could mask real incompatibilities causing subtle quality regressions. We'll include opt-in strict mode to fail onboarding if strict checks fail.
acceptance_criteria: Onboarding pipeline runs a tokenizer compatibility step that verifies token counts for a canonical set of chat templates across 3 sequence lengths: short(64), median(512), long(2048)
Performance profile JSON for onboarded models includes tokenization_overhead_ms and tokenizer_checksum fields
A documented shim exists that normalizes role delimiters and common special markers without altering semantic tokens for >95% of templates
Unit and integration tests added to pipeline that reproduce an earlier reported off-by-one prefix cache bug and assert regression is fixed
A canary rollout of the shim is performed and monitored for 72 hours with roll-back playbook documented
work_logs: 2026-01-11 - Maya Chen: Investigated three onboarding failures; root cause traced to changes in pretokenizer normalization for Unicode joiners and emoji clusters.

2026-01-14 - Arjun Patel: Reproduced mismatch in a local harness with model v3.1 vs v3.1-patched tokenizer; confirmed template delimiter '<|role|>' sometimes tokenizes to two subtokens on v3.1-patched.
2026-01-22 - Maya Chen: Prototype shim implemented that maps canonical role markers to control tokens before tokenization; initial perf impact < 0.6ms per request on 512 seq.
2026-01-28 - Sofia Martinez (PM): Reviewed acceptance criteria and requested tokenization_overhead be added to performance dashboards and published profile schema.
2026-02-02 - Maya Chen: Pulled request for design review and added test matrix for emoji/ZWJ/RTL cases.
design_notes: Shim design is two-stage: pre-tokenization marker normalization (lossless for ASCII markers) + post-tokenization alignment check comparing expected token indices for template placeholders.
Strict mode will fail onboarding early and surface a diff artifact (expected_token_sequence vs observed_token_sequence) to the PRD pipeline artifact store.
Fallback behavior for Dedicated/Private: expose config flag 'tokenizer_compatibility_mode' with values [strict, permissive, shim-only] to respect enterprise rollout constraints.
test_plan: Add unit tests for sample templates that include emojis, ZWJ, and combining diacritics; assert token counts stable across pinned versions.
Add integration test to onboarding flow that runs tokenizer compatibility job and fails if checksum changes exceed threshold.
Create performance microbenchmark measuring tokenization_overhead_ms across GPUs and CPU-backed tokenizers; include representative batch sizes.
Manual canary: onboard model to 'onboarding-canary' catalog, verify runtime traces for 48h, then widen to 72h before publishing profile.

Need sign-off from privacy/compliance for storing tokenization diffs in artifact store (security review flagged in previous run)
